title: Long Time No See
subtitle: Even after all I've seen, I will stop by the riverbank to watch the swaying of the little reed.

items.text: Mei Tree, Zhu County
The rising mist blurs everyone's vision, including that of a terrified, fleeing Critter.
A hand reaches in and lifts it up with ease, saving it from falling into the growing cracks.
She remembers when they first met. She had been just as miserable then as she is now.
A burning ozone smell hangs in the air. Paper Heron sits beneath the Mei tree and looks up.
The lightning is gone. She sighs in relief, then glances toward her feet.

items.speaker: Critter
items.text: *whimper*
A black fuzzball, weakened from multiple lightning strikes. Paper Heron looks down at it, pity welling up in her for the creature, despite everything.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Psps, come here, little one, come.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: My master always said we should remember the good done to us and find ways to repay it.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: You drew that lightning to the Mei tree and freed me from my seal. Though it was an accident, I have reaped its benefits, and for that, I must give you my thanks.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I have nothing of value save the Method. Here.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Now, be on your way.
She releases the struggling Critter, and it runs swiftly into the distant grass before vanishing from sight.
Paper Heron raises her head. Another figure is walking toward her through the mist.
The editor studies this new woman with a familiar face, cautious not to make the same mistake.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Paper Heron? Is that you?

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Is it really you?

items.speaker: Mule
items.text: Whinny ...
The old mule, inexplicably safe despite all the calamity, trots over and whinnies affectionately.
Paper Heron pats its head and smiles at Reed.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Yes, Reedit. It's the real me, this time.
Restaurant, Zhu County
The restaurant by the lake has only just opened for the day, but it's already packed with customers.
Visitors are willing to pay extra to see this new lake that appeared overnight.

items.speaker: Neighbor I
items.text: What did I tell you? This place is blessed. So many bright talents!

items.speaker: Neighbor I
items.text: See those reporters? We're gonna be on TV.

items.speaker: Neighbor II
items.text: So much for peace and quiet. I don't get it. What's so special about an old tree and a lake, anyway?

items.speaker: Waiter
items.text: Look on the bright side. Uncle Lǐ's been thinking about getting into the food business lately. With all these visitors, I bet he'll be moving into a big new house in no time. Isn't that right, Lǐ?

items.speaker: Neighbor I
items.text: Haha, sure is. When I've got the place settled, I'll have all of you over for a night of mahjong.

items.speaker: Waiter
items.text: We'll be there, and we won't go easy on you at the table.

items.speaker: Neighbor I
items.text: Do your worst. Hah-hah!
Guests at the corner tables take turns stealing conspicuous glances in their direction.
The waiter hurries over and sets down a plate of Fuliji Roast Chicken.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Thank you.

items.speaker: Waiter
items.text: Here on a visit? You don't look like you're from around here.

items.speaker: Waiter
items.text: We've been getting a lot of visitors lately. Just a heads-up: Watch out for the tourist traps, eh? Some of the souvenirs in the gift shops are pure rubbish.

items.speaker: Waiter
items.text: Ah, just look at that sword. Exactly what I mean. What a shame. Better off spending your money on local cuisine, I'd say.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Appreciated! We just tried the duck and snail stew. Maybe Bāo Zhěng's fish next?
The waiter turns away. Paper Heron taps the sword gently, but any sound it might make doesn't rise above the chatter of the restaurant.
She lets her hand linger over the fractured blade, then picks up their conversation.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: So, what did you want to tell me, Reedie?

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Err, it's not a big deal really. I just wanted to say it in person.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I'm sorry, Heron.
The words pour out bitter and regretful.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I shouldn't have fallen for Rén's trick. I knew something was off about her, but I-I guess I got greedy.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: If you hadn't come to my rescue in time, I ...

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: There, there. It's over now. We needn't worry about what's in the past.
She picks up the sword playfully, weighs it in her hand, then sets it down.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Long ago, Qi flowed strong in the world, surging and rolling like ocean waves. But now, it has quieted.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: It no longer has the force to shake the plains or topple mountains, and the spells drawn from its power have lost much of their might.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Lǎnzhū's power is much the same. That's why things didn't go Rén's way, even though she awakened the beast.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: When Lǎnzhū was strong, Rén could draw out its Qi to strengthen herself.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: But the flow of its Qi changed course. It draws in Qi rather than letting it flow out. A necessary balance. This is the Way.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Lǎnzhū is unlikely to cause any disasters for a long time to come. You needn't worry.
She leans forward and offers a hand of comfort to Reed.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Thanks to you, everything's finally settled. Though I can't help but take a little of the credit. I did do my best to guide you here.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Hm?

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Hold on, so, then you really were the one who guided me here? You wanted me to set Rén free from the seal?
Paper Heron lets the question hang in the air, offering only a knowing smile at first.
Then she speaks, her answer delicately pruned and insightful.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: When I saw your post on the forum, I knew that you were a Yao, but I couldn't be sure of what you'd do until you showed up in person.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Just like Mayfly, I knew you would take any risk to find the Method, and I realized Rén would seize on your desire and exploit it.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: You wouldn't be put off by what you saw in the Wind Knots; I knew you'd see it through to the end.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: So when Rén took my name to approach you on the forum, I didn't stop her, just like I didn't stop her from releasing Lǎnzhū.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: She would only be returning Qi to its rightful place, not disturbing it.
Her voice drops. After a brief pause, she continues.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: One gains, and the other loses. In the end, what's lost returns to where it is needed, and thus balance is maintained.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Were it not for your resolve, none of this would have come to pass.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: And because all who took part in this—you, Rén, me—stood by each of our choices to the end ...

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: What started hundreds of years ago could at last come to its rightful end.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: So you see, there's no need to apologize. All unfolded as fate intended.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I see.
Reed lets out a long breath. Her grass blades wilt on her head.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I haven't found longevity, but at least I found a story worth telling.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: That's good enough for me.
She can't hide the sting of regret in her voice, but she buries it as best she can.
Yet Paper Heron seizes on it.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: There's a little more to it, actually.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: In the spring after Mayfly's death, a green shoot grew from the place where she last stood.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: When winter came, it withered, but in each following spring, a sprout grew anew.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: You mean I'm ...?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: In a way, Mayfly's wish has been fulfilled.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Yeah.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I like this little epilogue.
Reed smiles as she closes her notebook.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I'm planning to write a couple more stories before winter comes.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I hope the "Reed" that sprouts next year likes them too.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Hmm.
She frowns playfully.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I must say, you're quite inquisitive for a reed.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: You'd likely make an excellent Daoist. Were you born in my time, many would have wanted you as their student.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: How about I—

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Thanks for the offer, but I've always wanted to be a commissioning editor. I think I've had enough of Daoism for one lifetime!
They both laugh for a long while. Reed composes herself first.
She thinks for a moment, then extends an invitation.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: But how about we take a walk around the Mei tree again?
Two figures approach the Mei tree. One crouches low; the other stands nearby.
Paper Heron looks up at the tree full of red blossoms and pats the bark as if greeting an old friend.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: This old thing will soon bloom more beautifully than ever.
The editor examines the stone bricks arranged around the tree, apparently recovered from some old houses that collapsed years ago.
A half-buried stone catches her attention.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: This is ...
She bends down and brushes away the layer of dirt covering its face.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Come on, Reedie.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: We'll still have some time if we take a shortcut to the streets.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Oh, sure!
The editor runs a few steps to keep up with her companion.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I've gotta report back to the office soon, tomorrow or at least by the day after.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: What about you? What're you gonna do?
Paper Heron tilts her head, gesturing toward a tall building in the distance.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I'll keep traveling. I seem to have missed a great deal over these last centuries.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: And, you know, my taste seems to have restored a little. Perhaps I'll search for a place with good food and stay there for a half-month.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I'd love to join you, if I still have time, that is.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: You'll still be on the forum, right? The same account?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Of course, and there's a friend I'd like you to meet, hm?

items.speaker: Cat
items.text: Meow.
The lake lies quiet as the wind laps gently over it, now a place where small creatures can gather to rest beneath the shade.
Paper Heron scoops up the fur ball and strokes its sleek coat.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Hey, little one. Are you from around here?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: How about some fish for supper, hm?
Seeing the cat lounge contentedly beside them, Reed rests her hand on its back as well.
She remembers her last question.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: A friend, huh? Someone else you met on the forum? Who are they?

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Any idea what kinda food they like? There's a couple restaurants around here that look good.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: You needn't worry. He'll be grateful to eat anything, and in fact, you already know him.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Last time, the seal took away my sense of taste, but his, at least, seems fine.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: He will have awakened by now. We can discuss it on the forum later.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I have to say, the Internet is quite amazing, connecting people from all corners of the globe.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: It sure is.
The editor gazes at the silver line where the lake meets the sky.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: *blow*
She raises her arms, stretching her tense body.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: So I got all worked up for nothing. But I guess I shouldn't complain.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: There's no cataclysm, no raging beast, just a tree, a lake, and a gentle breeze over a quiet little path.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Indeed.
She watches the fish as they bob up from the lake, surfacing one moment, diving deep the next.
One jumps up and vanishes away the moment it hits the water.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: It was all but a splash in the pond.
